gallery.title: File:St Mary Redcliffe Church, Bristol, BRO Picbox-7-StMR-9, 1250x1250.jpg
gallery.artist: Unknown, created before 1850s.  Image from the collection of Bristol Record Office
gallery.source: St Mary Redcliffe Church, Bristol, BRO Picbox-7-StMR-9, 1250x1250
gallery.description: Black and white etching of St Mary Redcliffe church, Bristol, England, published before 1850. The view is from the northwest, showing the tower at the west end with its distinctive truncated spire and the elaborate system of steps to access the church by the North Porch. In the foreground are eight figures climbing the steps towards the church and a cattle drover.

gallery.source: St Mary Redcliffe Church, Bristol, BRO Picbox-7-StMR-33, 1250x1250
gallery.description: Black and white floorplan of St Mary Redcliffe church, Bristol, England, published before 1850. It shows the traditional cruciform shape of the church, with the large west tower and hexagonal north Porch. Also on the plan are faint lines showing the shapes of the vaulted arch ceilings between each column and wall.

gallery.source: St. Mary Redcliffe Church (37084222731)
gallery.description: St. Mary Redcliffe Church, Bristol, 13 September 2017. Claimed to be the largest parish church in England and built as a rval to the cathedral. Mostly late 14th Century Perpendicular but late 13th/early 14th Century Decorated south aisle and south transept, north and south porches, and tower, Victorian (1872) spire. Pictured is the 1593 Cope chest for vestments.

gallery.filename: Bristol, St Mary Redcliffe church, East window (48694712611).jpg
gallery.title: File:Bristol, St Mary Redcliffe church, East window (48694712611).jpg
gallery.credit: Bristol, St Mary Redcliffe church, East window
gallery.source: Bristol, St Mary Redcliffe church, East window (48694712611)
gallery.description:
The easternmost window of the church in the Lady Chapel can be seen as a blaze of colour upon entering the church.
It depicts the Nativity in the upper half, with the Deposition in the lower half. The tracery contains angels in red and yellow.

Glass is by Harry Stammers, early 1960s.

gallery.filename: Bristol, St Mary Redcliffe church, window n.III (48694882937).jpg
gallery.title: File:Bristol, St Mary Redcliffe church, window n.III (48694882937).jpg
gallery.credit: Bristol, St Mary Redcliffe church, window n.III
gallery.source: Bristol, St Mary Redcliffe church, window n.III (48694882937)
gallery.description:
North window in the Lady Chapel depicting the Virgin and Child, below which Eve stands with the apple. They are surrounded by people in various costumes, some Elizabethan, some modern, and Saints including St Margaret, St Catherine and St Francis of Assisi, and various musicians above.
It is based on the line from The Magnificat "All generations shall call me blessed"

Glass by Harry Stammers, 1965.
